en:
Tsk, damn pests...! Why the hell
do I have to play nice and go
exploring ruins with these
Federation lackeys...!
Phew, I believe we discussed\nthis many times before the\nexploration began.

This ship's hull belongs to the
Federation, but with people
from so many different
organizations, it is something
quite distinct from them.
I believe it is wise to cooperate\nfor the sake of our respective\ngoals.
Even so, I have no obligation to\ncooperate with you lot!
Huh? Pavine, aren't you\ncoming? I was looking forward\nto exploring together, mya~!
Ugh...
I-It's only this once! You damn\npests!
Yay! Let's go, mya!

Pavine is actually quite kind to
children, in his own way. He's
quite good at looking after
them.

Yes, it seems he occasionally
joins Relia and the others for
games of hide-and-seek on the
ship.
Mirage, Captain, hurry up, hurry\nup!
Myamyam!?
Myaaaaaaaah!
Whoa!
...Phew, I finally made it out.
Hmm? But why did the door\nsuddenly open, mya?
Wait, could you be...?
What is it?
My... Myaaaaaaah!
Ah! This is the memory of when\nI first met Edge, mya!

I mistakenly thought the
researchers had found me and
ran away. And then, after
that...
W-waaaah! Don't come any\ncloser, mya!
Myaaaaaah!
Leave this to us and get back!

Edge was so cool back then~.
He appeared right in front of
me just as I was about to be
eaten by an experimental
creature...
Tsk. You Earthlings really have\nno respect for the protection\nof primitive planets, do you?

The Captain is wrong! Edge
was just saving me after I got
captured!! He didn't do
anything wrong!
You're flaunting advanced tech\nweapons on a planet with such\na low civilization level.
Human lives were being\nthreatened. I believe the use of\nweapons was unavoidable.

Besides, the Primitive Planet
Protection Treaty didn't even
exist in Edge's era, so no rules
were broken.
Hmph. Nothing but excuses\nfrom you little pests.

Do you think I won't find out
how this ends? You got tricked
by the director and ended up
in a real mess, didn't you? Heh
heh heh.
That couldn't be helped!! Edge\nthought he could protect the\nEarth of the Professors!!
And instead, you just drove it\ntoward destruction. What a\npain.

Even without a treaty, any idiot
could see what happens if you
hand antimatter to fools with
no knowledge, right?
...B-but, even so, at that time...\nEdge was...!
Quite right. Pavine, don't you\nknow better than anyone that\narguing here is pointless?
Besides, it's not as if you want\nto make a young child this sad.
Tsk...
Meracle, are you alright?
Yeah...

Captain, I recommend we
cancel this exploration and
return for now. What do you
think?
No, let's keep exploring.\nCaptain, Mirage, I'm okay!\nThank you!
Hey, Pavine. Why do you talk\nso badly about everyone?
Huh? It's obvious. It's because\nthose Federation bastards are\nnothing but scum.
What?!

If the Federation is involved, I
won't hold back, dammit! This
is your final warning, you idiots.
Hand over Relia!
Why is there a space\nbattleship in this sector...?
Just how far are you going to\ngo?! This is a violation of the\nCFNZ!

Appearing a battleship over an
uncolonized planet... That's a
massive violation of the
Uncolonized Planet Protection
Treaty.
They were the ones who\nviolated it first!
Dammit! You idiots, capture\nRelia, now!
Aaaaaaaah!!
Sh-shit! Dammit!!
Chronos Soldier: Shall I report\nthis to His Excellency the\nGeneral?

Mind your own business, you
worm! She might still be
nearby! Search everywhere
with everything you've got!!
Brother Pavi, things have taken\na turn for the worse!

As if things could get any
worse, you little worm! And
don't call me that in front of
the army!
Ah, ah, sorry, Brother Pavi!\n...Oh.
Enough! Now, what happened?

It looks like one of the Phase
Guns we provided to the
Eitalon leader was stolen by a
resident of this planet!
What!?

We found a strange woman in
Meedock claiming to be an
inventor stole it, but she has
no intention of returning it, no
matter what we say.
I think if we sneak into her\nhouse in the middle of the\nnight, we could take it back...

Stop it, idiot! That woman is a
civilian with no connection to
this! Are you going to act just
like those damn Federation
scum!?
Brother Pavi...
...Prepare some Forl. Negotiate\nto buy it back at a high price.

Tsk, I was against providing our
weapons to lowlife scum like
Eitalon from the very
beginning...!
Yeah. They've even been\nattacking villages that have\nnothing to do with us...

Anyway, get to the
negotiations now! If they
dismantle them improperly, the
whole town could blow up!

You're surprisingly
humanitarian. Especially
considering you attacked the
royal capital with a starship.

Those who arm themselves and
prepare for battle are different
from civilians who do not. Can't
you even grasp that, you idiot?
You seemed really close with\nHal, too. Are you friends?

He's just a local brat. Since
we're from the same planet, I
was tasked with looking after
him after joining the military.
I know that! That's what you\ncall a childhood friend! Just\nlike Edge and Reimi, mya!
Don't say it in such a creepy\nway, you idiot! We're just from\nthe same planet.
Well, though that planet is no\nlonger under Kronos's control...
It was cast aside. By the damn\nKronos government.

Being in the frontier, those
unhappy with the Federation
treaty gathered and launched
a massive rebellion against the
Kronos government.

The Kronos government
struggled to suppress the
rebellion, so the Federation
intervened under the guise of
helping. By then, they had
control.

Now, it's just a playground for
Federation bottom-feeders to
vent their frustrations―a damn
exhibition of crime.
That's... horrible...

That's why I put my faith in
that person... General Alma! I
knew that she could wipe
those Federation fools out!

This is the path I have chosen!
I will eliminate anyone who
stands in her way, no matter
what it takes!
Even if it means violating that\ndamn Uninhabited Planet\nProtection Treaty!
If it's Kronos, does that mean\nPavine's home planet is in\nSector Kappa?

No, it's Iota. It was located at
coordinates relatively close to
Faykreed and the Federation's
5th Deep Space Base.
Which means...
This kid?
Yes, Cliff. They're quite weak,\nbut it doesn't look like their life\nis in danger.
An Earthling.
It appears so.

Data from the escape pod
suggests they were victims of
the recent battle with Ardion
at Federation Space Base 17.
So this brat is another victim\nof war...

Yes. In our era, the Federation
has been at war with an
organization called the Ardion
Empire for a long time.

it is not uncommon to discover
escape pods from civilians
caught up in the war while we
are navigating.
This Girl... she looks like\nsomeone I know...

It's Maria. This is a memory
from seven years ago, so Cliff
and I would have been much
younger, wouldn't we?

S-S-Seven years ago!? Even
so, Mirage and Cliff don't look
like they've changed a bit at
all, myah...
I'll take that as a compliment.

Even after centuries, the
Federation is still stuck in
power struggles... In the end,
it's just civilians who suffer.
Damn pests...

Poor thing. And she's so small,
too. The Federation and Ardion
should keep their power
struggles to themselves.
It's always the civilians who\nend up paying the price.
...Is that why you founded this\norganization?
It's nothing that grand. I just\nhate following people I don't\nrespect.
There's no need to be shy. ...At\nleast not in front of me.
I'll punch you.
Hehe...
...Sorry, but could I ask you to\nlook after this kid?
I understand, Cliff.
You're reading that email again,\naren't you?
Oh, Mirage. Don't sneak up on\nme like that. Is the kid doing\nokay?
Yes, her vitals are stable. I\nthought I'd use this time to\nrecalculate our flight path.
Recalculate the route?

We can't fly through dangerous
sectors with her. I'll find the
shortest, safest route back to
Claustro.
That's alright with you, isn't it,\nCliff?
Yeah, go ahead. Sorry, Mirage. I\nhadn't thought that far ahead.
I figured you'd be too busy\nrereading that email to focus\non anything else.
You've got me figured out,\ndon't you?

A report on Sector ι's reality
and the Federation's lawless
zone. It was our very first job,
after all.
Sector ι! Do you know the\nfuture of my home planet?!

Sector ι is quite vast, so I
cannot say for certain if this
refers to your home planet,
Pavine.

However, Quark once took
requests from locals seeking
independence and even filed
lawsuits against the Federation
regarding autonomy.
...And how did that turn out?
Unfortunately...
Ha, I figured. There's no way\nthe Federation would grant\nsomething like that so easily.
Why not?! Everyone just wants\nto decide things for\nthemselves!

...One exception leads to
another. If a vital military
stronghold demands autonomy,
it'll be a disaster.
The trial has concluded, but we\nat Quark do not believe the\nmatter is settled.

If individual victories are
difficult to achieve, we will
unite those factions to win
complete autonomy.
That is the method Quark has\nadopted, learned from that\nvery defeat.

So you think if those seeking
independence gather across
star systems instead of just
planets, you can actually stand
against the Federation?

Yes, we have already
successfully achieved
independence in several star
systems.
That's amazing, mya! Since\nMirage's era is 200 years from\nnow...

It's hard to save Pavine's
friends now, but their
great-great-great-grandchildren
will live happily, mya!

Wars only cause innocent
civilians to suffer. That is why
we resolve things through the
law. This is the path we have
chosen.

Hmph... Are you trying to tell
me, to my face, that the future
isn't something to be given up
on?
Is that not allowed?
Hmph, everyone has their own\nway of living. Do as you please.
Actually, the person who made\na request to us from Sector ι\nis named Oakville...

Oh, wait, that is a story of a
future you all have yet to see.
Please forget I said anything,
Captain.

This story has concluded. We
plan to release various other
stories in the future. Please
look forward to them.
